topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and mutation progression
topics.groupedBecause: This section introduces the lecture structure, learning outcomes, and foundational framework of cancer hallmarks and multi-step mutation progression.

topics.label: Deregulation of growth signaling pathways in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how mutations in cell-surface receptors and downstream intracellular cascades drive sustained proliferative signaling and growth factor independence.

topics.label: Blocks in terminal cell differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer cells fail to withdraw from the cell cycle and differentiate, illustrated in hematopoietic malignancies and intestinal epithelium.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how mutations in p53 and alterations in the balance between pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins prevent cancer cells from undergoing programmed cell death.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, senescence, and cellular stress signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss telomere biology, mechanisms of telomerase reactivation, senescence, and the role of p53 in coordinating cell fate decisions under cellular stress.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the alterations in cancer cell metabolism, including aerobic glycolysis, tissue-specific metabolic profiles, and mutations that generate oncometabolites.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the angiogenic switch and the mechanisms by which growing tumors stimulate new blood vessel formation to overcome hypoxia and nutrient limitation.

topics.label: Mechanisms, dissemination, and genetics of metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the metastatic cascade, factors governing metastatic efficiency and organotropism, and the genomic characteristics of secondary tumors.

topics.label: Lecture summary and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: This section concludes the lecture with a summary of cancer hallmarks, recommended further reading, and closing administrative remarks.
